question.problem:
$$
{A}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{A}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Find the matrix $C$ given that $B=\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\},$ and the coordinates of the matrix $C$ relative to $B$ are $[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

current_example.problem:
Consider the polynomials $p_1(t)$ and $p_2(t),$ given by

$$
p_1(t)=3+2t, \qquad
	p_2(t)=-t+t^2.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $\mathcal{B}=\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14159472/assets/12219bddf4479a5d4578e022bae46d09b38b2499486f3ee59eafb30c2ed1f074.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Any vector in $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14159472/assets/41a4f8d266d67bbe48e91aefa7b4a09f53143b3218ea68b1df9d2ee9e1f373d5.svg)

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =4\cdot (3+2t)+(-3)\cdot (-t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =12+8t+3t-3{t}^{2} \\  & =12+11t-3{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
